tasks.title: Customers by city
tasks.statement: Output the city and the number of customers in it: `city`, `n` (GROUP BY city). Order by city; the NULL city comes first.
tasks.hint: GROUP BY collects rows into groups, and the aggregate is computed in each group.

tasks.title: Orders by status
tasks.statement: Output `status` and the number of orders `n` in each status; order by status.

tasks.title: Products by category
tasks.statement: Output `category` and the number of products `n`; order by category.

tasks.title: Sum by category
tasks.statement: Output `category` and the total stock `stock` as `total_stock`; order by category.

tasks.title: Average price in a category
tasks.statement: Output `category` and the average price (ROUND to an integer) as `avg_price`; order by category.

tasks.title: Minimum and maximum in a group
tasks.statement: Output `category`, `min_price` and `max_price` for each category; order by category.

tasks.title: Revenue by customer
tasks.statement: Output `customer_id` and the total of all their orders `revenue`; order by customer_id.

tasks.title: Revenue leaders
tasks.statement: Output `customer_id` and `revenue` for the three customers with the largest order totals (the totals are distinct); order by revenue descending.

tasks.title: Two grouping columns
tasks.statement: Output `customer_id`, `status` and the number of orders `n` for each pair; order by customer_id, status.

tasks.title: Grouping by expression
tasks.statement: Output the order month `strftime('%Y-%m', created)` as `month` and the number of orders `n`; order by month.
tasks.hint: You can group by a computed expression or its alias.

tasks.title: Revenue by month
tasks.statement: Output `month` (YYYY-MM) and the order total `revenue` per month; order by month.

tasks.title: WHERE before grouping
tasks.statement: Compute the total of paid orders (`status = 'paid'`) per customer: `customer_id`, `revenue`; order by customer_id. WHERE runs before GROUP BY.

tasks.title: HAVING
tasks.statement: Output the cities with at least two customers: `city`, `n` (`HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2`). Order by city.

tasks.title: HAVING on a sum
tasks.statement: Output `customer_id` and `revenue` for customers whose total revenue exceeds 10000; order by customer_id.

tasks.title: WHERE and HAVING together
tasks.statement: Among orders that are not cancelled (`status <> 'cancelled'`), find customers with two or more orders: `customer_id`, `n`; order by customer_id.

tasks.title: Duplicates
tasks.statement: Find brands that occur in several products: `brand` and the number of products `n` (`HAVING COUNT(*) > 1`; ignore the NULL brand); order by brand.

tasks.title: The NULL group
tasks.statement: How many customers are there in each city, including "no city"? NULL forms its own group. Output `city`, `n`; order by n descending, then by city.

tasks.title: Sorting by an aggregate
tasks.statement: Output `category` and the number of products `n`, the most numerous categories first; on ties, order by category.

tasks.title: COUNT DISTINCT in a group
tasks.statement: Output `status` and the number of distinct customers in it, `customers_n`; order by status.

tasks.title: Sold by product
tasks.statement: Output `product_id` and how many units were sold, `sold` (`SUM(qty)`); order by product_id.

tasks.title: Revenue by product
tasks.statement: Output `product_id` and the revenue `SUM(qty * price)` as `revenue`; the most profitable first, on ties by product_id.

tasks.title: Grouping with JOIN
tasks.statement: Output the category name and its revenue: `category`, `revenue` (order_items JOIN products). Order by revenue descending.

tasks.title: Customers and their revenue
tasks.statement: Output the customer's `name` and the total of their orders `revenue` (JOIN customers, GROUP BY c.id); order by revenue descending, then by name.

tasks.title: With zeros
tasks.statement: Output `name` and the number of orders `n` for ALL customers, including those with no orders (LEFT JOIN, COUNT over o.id). Order by n descending, then by name.
tasks.hint: COUNT(o.id) does not count NULL, so customers without orders get 0.

tasks.title: A list in a group
tasks.statement: Output `status` and a comma-separated list of order ids `ids` (group_concat), in id order: first a subquery with ORDER BY. Order by status.

tasks.title: Conditional sum in a group
tasks.statement: Output `customer_id`, `paid_sum` (the total of paid orders) and `all_sum` (the total of all orders) for each customer; order by customer_id.

tasks.title: Classes in a group
tasks.statement: Output the price class `tier` (`'дёшево'` below 1000, otherwise `'дорого'`) and the number of products `n`: group by a CASE expression. Order by tier.

tasks.title: Category share
tasks.statement: Output `category` and its share of the product count in percent (ROUND to an integer) as `pct`: `100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products)`. Order by pct descending, then category.

tasks.title: Most expensive in a category
tasks.statement: Output the title of the most expensive product for each category: a subquery with MAX(price) by category and a join. Columns `category`, `title`; order by category.

tasks.title: Number in GROUP BY
tasks.statement: Output `category` and `COUNT(*)` as `n`, grouping and sorting by column numbers (`GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1`).

tasks.title: HR: by department
tasks.statement: HR database. Output `dept_id`, the number of employees `n` and the average salary (ROUND to an integer) `avg_salary` by department, excluding employees without a department; order by dept_id.

tasks.title: HR: payroll by department
tasks.statement: HR database. Output the department name (JOIN departments) and the payroll `payroll`; order by payroll descending.

tasks.title: HR: large departments
tasks.statement: HR database. Output the names of departments with 4 or more employees, and their count `n`; order by name.

tasks.title: HR: by grade
tasks.statement: HR database. Output `grade` and the average salary (ROUND to an integer) `avg_salary`; order by avg_salary descending.

tasks.title: HR: who has how many subordinates
tasks.statement: HR database. Output `boss_id` and the number of subordinates `n`; only for those who have any; order by n descending, then boss_id.

tasks.title: HR: hires by year
tasks.statement: HR database. Output the hiring year `strftime('%Y', hired)` as `year` and the number of hires `n`; order by year.

tasks.title: School: a student's average score
tasks.statement: School database. Output `student_id` and the average score (ROUND to 2 decimals) `avg_score` over the records of 2024; order by avg_score descending, then student_id.

tasks.title: School: average by course
tasks.statement: School database. Output the course `title` and the average score for 2024 (ROUND to 2 decimals) as `avg_score`; only courses with grades; order by avg_score descending, then title.

tasks.title: School: top students
tasks.statement: School database. Output the `name` of students who have two or more top marks (fives) in 2024 (HAVING), and the number of fives `fives`; order by name.

tasks.title: School: records by year
tasks.statement: School database. Output `year` and the number of records `n`; order by year.

tasks.title: School: classes
tasks.statement: School database. Output `class` and the number of students `n`; order by class.

tasks.title: Movies: by genre
tasks.statement: Movie database. Output `genre`, the number of movies `n` and the average rating (ROUND to 2 decimals) `avg_rating` by genre; order by n descending, then genre.

tasks.title: Movies: directors
tasks.statement: Movie database. Output the director's `name` and the number of their movies `n`; order by n descending, then name.

tasks.title: Movies: decades
tasks.statement: Movie database. Output the decade `year / 10 * 10` as `decade` and the number of movies `n`; order by decade.

tasks.title: Movies: countries
tasks.statement: Movie database. Output the director's country and the total budget of the movies `total_budget` (NULL budgets are not counted); order by total_budget descending.
